Triangle polar vertices have exact shoelace area 3; all quadrilaterals admit positive diagonal ratios and their normalized polar is contained in a square with all-four-strip equality equivalent to \(s=t=1\). For \(n\ge5\), Brunn–Minkowski area(D)>=4area(P) and symmetric Blaschke–Santaló area(D)area(D^circ)<=pi^2 prove strictness. Exact-rational regressions check examples; no numerical sample is used as universal proof.

originality.rationale: Winter 2026 proves the universal flag inequality but explicitly leaves equality unresolved. The exact planar classification is not covered by the closest full-text original studies: the Eggleston/Makai result is a lower bound, and the Meyer–Reisner polygon volume product uses a different centered polar.
